# ↪️ Pull Request This PR aims to fulfill requirements made in #3355 -- that is to port the jsonld asset v1 code into a v2 jsonld transformer Closes #3355 ## 💻 Examples take a look at the [index.html][example] that is used for the jsonld integration test ## 🚨 Test instructions Run the following: `yarn workspace @parcel/integration-tests test -g jsonld` The integration test file for jsonld is defined [here][test] ## ✔️ PR Todo - [x] Added/updated unit tests for this change - [x] Filled out test instructions (In case there aren't any unit tests) - [x] Included links to related issues/PRs ## 🐛 Issues - [x] the jsonld is not outputting the json data back into the built [index.html][example] file in the proper format - the data injected into the index.html isn't a pure json object but is wrapped in JS code - now a `
` is being injected into the script tag where the jsonld object used to be - [x] unable to get the `publicURL` config option from the available objects passed into the transform object - `--public-url https://place.holder/` is being passed to the `parcel build` command, however, logs do not show it appearing anywhere - update fom @DeMoorJasper: url replacement occurs further down the line after packaging and therefore no longer needs to happen inside the transformer - [x] the `asset.addURLDependency()` is returning a number, which causes `urlJoin()` to throw an error - this logic is ported directly from v1 code, so it seems that the addURLDependency has changed what it returns for v2 changes?? - update from @DeMoorJasper: the number being returned will eventually be replaced by the new asset path during the naming stage, therefore, replacing the old asset path with the number is sufficient - [x] unit tests are failing because the jsonld transformer is not part of the [package.json](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/v2/packages/configs/default/package.json) list - It seems I am meant to add it to the list in order to get that unit test to pass. - However, I need to publish the transformer package first - Unfortunately and not surprisingly, I do not have permissions to publish the new @parcel/transformer-jsonld package - [x] integration test is failing because it is using an old method to test the bundle - [x] the [integration test][test] uses the function `assertBundles()` which is not seeing the expected .png and .jpeg dependencies, however, when using the local parcel cli to build the [index.html][example], those image assets get pulled through to the dist folder - 🤦‍♂ accidentally removed the code that parses the jsonld object -- put it back in and the images are getting pulled through again and the integration test is seeing them - [x] unable to figure out how to assert the transformer output for an asset in the integration test [example]: https://github.com/isaacadams/parcel/blob/feature/v2-jsonld-transformer/packages/core/integration-tests/test/integration/schema-jsonld/index.html [test]: https://github.com/isaacadams/parcel/blob/feature/v2-jsonld-transformer/packages/core/integration-tests/test/schema-jsonld.js

issue_context.title: Parcel 2: JSONLD transformer
issue_context.body:
Create the `@parcel/transformer-jsonld` package in `packages/transforms/jsonld`. This package is a Parcel 2 transform plugin for JSONLD. It should be based on the `JSONLDAsset` from Parcel 1.

The `@parcel/transformer-jsonld` package is responsible for the following things:

* Parsing and collecting dependencies
* Rewriting urls to dependencies
* Compiling back to JSON

review_comments:
- parcel v1 seems to inject the json object write back into the script tag on the html page
- The only difference is that any asset paths that was in the jsonld are now updated with the new asset paths
- However, my local parcel injects the json object wrapped in javascript code with `module.exports=` and syntax like that

Yeah that makes sense... the json transformer will convert it into js.

We have to figure out a way to ignore this in some way, I think we were gonna query parameters for this like in https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/pull/4209

But that PR also implements the query param support so maybe it should get merged asap so this can output json?
We could also put the JSON transformer on a named pipeline instead and insert that pipeline to JSON imports in JS (just as we do with url dependencies and `url:`)
That's also a possibility and probably a better option in this case (as it will unblock this PR)
@DeMoorJasper & @mischnic let me know if there is anything I can do to help get this PR unblocked or if there is another PR I should be keeping my eyes on.
You can use named pipelines for now. So nothing should be blocking this PR :)
Is there something I need to add to the code here in order to use the named pipelines? Or are you saying the code is fine how it is because the named pipelines will pick it up.

change the `"*.{json,json5}": ["@parcel/transformer-json"],` into something like `"js:*.{json,json5}": ["@parcel/transformer-json"],` (in the default config)

Than `js:./something.json` will parse json into js and `url:./something.json` will just copy the json to the output directory and in your case not transform jsonld beyond your transformer
